sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Cape Coral?
sections.html:
Know which Lee County office controls each piece of the sale, then choose between listing, selling yourself and a direct cash sale. Cape Coral homes are assessed, billed and recorded through Lee County, so the county's calendar and fees matter as much as anything the city does.

Property values come from the Lee County Property Appraiser, whose office handles questions about assessments. Tax bills come from the Lee County Tax Collector, and the Clerk records the deed. Start by pulling your parcel record and your latest tax bill so you know what a buyer will see.

  • Check that the owner names on title match the people who will sign.
  • Look for open permits, liens or unpaid taxes.
  • Ask whether a lender, a tenant or an heir has a say in the timing.

sections.h2: What calendar does the Lee County Property Appraiser publish?
sections.html:
The office lists a yearly cycle that starts with January 1 as the assessment date and ends with tax bills in November. It also notes that applications for exemptions filed after March 1 may be granted for the following year, which matters if you buy or move late in the year.

Lee County Property Appraiser, dates to remember
WhenEvent
January 1Date of assessment for all properties
January and FebruaryApplications for exemptions are filed for the current year
March 1Deadline for all exemptions and agricultural classification
April 1Tangible personal property returns due
July 1Assessment rolls go to the Department of Revenue
AugustTRIM notices mailed; 25 days to petition the Value Adjustment Board on value
OctoberRolls certified for collection
NovemberTax Collector mails bills

The Property Appraiser also says owners may ask for an informal conference at any time during the year, which can settle a value question before it becomes an appeal.

sections.h2: How does the early-payment discount work in Lee County?
sections.html:
Paying early lowers the bill: 4 percent off in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, as the Property Appraiser's calendar prints it. The Department of Revenue prints the same schedule for the whole state.

Taxes turn delinquent on April 1. Tax certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1, and the certificate holder may not contact the owner to demand payment until 2 years after April 1 of the year of issuance, under section 197.432. The holder may apply for a tax deed after that 2-year period passes, with a $75 application fee.

For a seller, the lesson is simple: clear the balance before closing, or have the closing agent pay it from proceeds. A certificate on the property can delay a buyer's lender, and a buyer will ask about it.

sections.h2: What happens if the lender or the county is moving on the property?
sections.html:
Timelines are short once a judgment exists. A foreclosure final judgment directs the clerk to hold a public sale not less than 20 or more than 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer, per section 45.031. Notice is published for two consecutive weeks, and the high bidder posts 5 percent of the bid.

A separate path, the order to show cause under section 702.10, lets a lienholder ask for a quick hearing in a verified complaint. That hearing falls no sooner than the later of 20 days after the order is served or 45 days after the complaint is served. The statute presumes an owner-occupied residence when a homestead exemption appears on the latest roll.

  • Surplus funds: a final judgment must include notice of them, and owners should check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale.
  • Tax deed sales: homestead property carries an opening bid that includes half of the latest assessed value.
  • If either process has started, call a Florida attorney first.

sections.h2: Can squatters or a lapsed tenant affect my Cape Coral sale?
sections.html:
Yes, an occupant can delay closing, but Florida gives owners real tools. Under section 82.036 an owner or agent can file a verified Complaint to Remove Persons Unlawfully Occupying Residential Real Property with the sheriff, who serves a notice to vacate and puts the owner back in possession when conditions are met.

Those conditions include that no tenancy exists, the occupant is not family, the property is not open to the public, the owner has told them to leave and no litigation is pending. A false statement exposes the owner to damages, including statutory damages equal to triple the fair market rent plus costs and fees.

Adverse possession is a different matter. Section 95.18 requires 7 years of actual continued possession under a claim of title, payment of taxes and a return filed with the Property Appraiser. A person who lives in a house only on an adverse possession claim before filing that return commits trespass under the statute. Most vacant-house problems never reach that stage, but a vacant property is the one to watch.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs might apply to a Cape Coral homeowner?
sections.html:
Several, and some depend on age or service. A county or city may allow an extra homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older within an income limit, under section 196.075. Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a discount equal to the VA disability percentage, and a disabled ex-servicemember may receive a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.

A homeowner who may defer taxes should file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. Deferral covers the part of the bill above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Ask the Lee County offices which of these apply before you decide to sell under pressure.

sections.h2: What does it cost to put a deed on record?
sections.html:
The state tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and all parties to the document stay liable even if the contract assigns it to one side. Lee County follows the standard rate, since Miami-Dade is the lone exception.

The clerk adds recording charges under section 28.24: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus $1.00 for each name beyond four. Smaller trust-fund and technology charges apply on top. Ask the Lee County Clerk for a total before closing so nothing surprises you at the table.

A deed between spouses where the only consideration is a mortgage on the homestead, and divorce deeds for the marital home, fall under an exemption in section 201.02(7). A deed made for estate planning has no special exemption, according to the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Which county handles Cape Coral property taxes?
faqs.a: Lee County. The Lee County Property Appraiser sets values, the Lee County Tax Collector mails bills in November, and the Clerk records deeds.

faqs.q: When is the Lee County exemption deadline?
faqs.a: March 1. The Property Appraiser's date list says filings after that day may be granted for the following year, so file as early as you can once you own the home on January 1.

faqs.q: How long do I have to challenge my value?
faqs.a: 25 days from the mailing of the TRIM notice, which goes out in August, according to the Lee County Property Appraiser. An informal conference with the office is available at any time during the year.

faqs.q: What if there are unpaid taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: They must be cleared for clean title, usually from sale proceeds at closing. Bills are delinquent from April 1, and tax certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1.

faqs.q: Can I remove someone living in my vacant Cape Coral house?
faqs.a: Possibly, through a sheriff removal complaint if the statutory conditions are met, such as no tenancy and no litigation. If anything is in doubt, ask an attorney before filing.
